a-cli.crash.autonomy: Allowed actions stay within active inherited lease action/root/spend/destructive/public limits; startup procedure exercises scope, expiry and revocation.
a-cli.scheduler.root: Scheduler root follows configured cluster/control root; explicitly opting out preserves requested legacy root.

a-cli.scheduler.capabilities: Efficient controller advertises self-repair but no frontend build; browser verification requires a passing dependency receipt and existing declared executable. Capacity zero means unlimited.
a-cli.scheduler.job: Canonical active job deduplication persists at most one active row per nonempty key.
a-cli.scheduler.claim: Claims return exact job/lease/host affinity; serialized admission obeys capacity, and scans past incompatible jobs without a fixed queue cap.
a-cli.scheduler.choose: Selected hosts are online and provide declared required capabilities; startup validates preference for healthy workstation over controller storage.
a-cli.scheduler.lease: New lease owns exactly the queued job on its selected host and cannot overlap another active writer in the same workspace.
a-cli.scheduler.load: Persisted host load equals durable active leases of leased/running jobs immediately after admission and completion.
a-cli.scheduler.stale: Every expired heartbeat marked stale removes advertised online availability and clears load.
a-cli.scheduler.expire: Expired leases no longer own a running job; restart recovery requeues the job and clears lease affinity.
a-cli.scheduler.roles: Planner/browser capability authority follows declared route role and phase rather than prompt mentions of verification.
a-cli.scheduler.worker: Local workers advertise explicit capacity even when idle and persist terminal job state matching actual execution with a terminal event.
a-cli.scheduler.environment: Actual child environment binds the job's authoritative control root without changing configured cluster root.
a-cli.scheduler.execute: Executable job success matches actual child return code; failed children cannot report completion.
a-cli.scheduler.threads: Unlimited worker attempts create independent thread/admission/completion channels; startup admits twelve overlapping owned attempts without a fixed threadpool ceiling.
a-cli.scheduler.lifecycle: Each worker lifecycle write persists its exact host/status/error; one-shot success/failure both stop and release the owned PID file.
a-cli.continuity.attempt: Successful action identities and evidence persist before restart suppresses duplicate completed attempts.
a-cli.continuity.recovery: Restart recovery retains completed action identities for safe continuation.
a-cli.continuity.verification: Transfers require target existence and size or hash verification.
a-cli.continuity.gpu-label: GPU controls classify destructive, stop, resume and start labels before inspection.
a-cli.continuity.gpu: GPU decisions enforce cost and capacity, preserve checkpoint preference and paid or destructive approval, and bound unchanged observations with a state-change override.
a-cli.scheduler.rehome: Shared queue recovery retains legacy lineage and leaves the mission-local database row unchanged.
a-cli.scheduler.queued: A queued delegated session keeps its step in progress without consuming attempts or acknowledging unfinished work.
a-cli.scheduler.unlimited-loop: Unlimited worker admission uses independent thread/claim channels without a fixed pool and preserves durable local completion.
a-cli.preferences.budget: Relative timers and objective deadlines override hour hints, persist a deadline and require continuous execution until blocked.
a-cli.preferences.continue: Delegated runtime activity pauses the mission loop to prevent repeated execution.
a-cli.preferences.poll: Continuous missions poll at a positive interval; pause mode uses no repeating interval.
a-cli.preferences.docs: Product missions completing with documentation-only changes become durably blocked with the specific missing-product-change reason.
a-cli.preferences.queue: Bundled worker resumes identify one active durable job with authoritative control root, workspace root and composer provenance.
a-cli.preferences.dispatch: Background dispatch suppresses duplicate owned active processes and queues cluster work from the authoritative mission store.
a-cli.preferences.pid: Windows process detection accepts only successful CSV output containing the requested PID; localized absence is not liveness.
a-cli.preferences.spawn: Detached mission children receive no interactive input and get a new POSIX session when the selected platform requires it.
a-cli.preferences.stop: Stopping a mission preserves terminal delegated history and stops only unfinished sessions.
a-cli.preferences.watchdog: Scoped one-shot watchdog passes preserve active ongoing loop identity and counts; ongoing passes retain own liveness.
a-cli.preferences.started: Successful mission starts persist their mission and requested relative timer.
a-cli.preferences.mark-dispatch: Mission state becomes running after permitted dispatch and blocked after a blocked receipt.
a-cli.preferences.compact: Compact mission action receipts preserve mission state and dispatch while omitting the full snapshot.
a-cli.preferences.cycle: Mission engine cycles forward the remaining enforced budget, continuous-mode handoff policy and an existing safe checkpoint.
